## TL;DR

Every mass carves a potential valley, $\Phi(r) = -GM/r$, and leaving it costs kinetic energy. This module compares three shapes of that valley: Earth's, which stops at a solid floor and sets the rocket equation; a Schwarzschild black hole's, which has no floor and fixes the ISCO, photon sphere and horizon at set fractions of its depth; and a binary system's double well with five Lagrange points. Two simulators let you rotate the surfaces and launch test orbits.
:::

Place a bowling ball on a stretched rubber sheet and it sags into a smooth conical dip. A marble rolled nearby no longer travels straight; it curves around the dip, orbits it, or spirals in.

That picture is a workable model of a **gravitational potential well**. Real gravity acts in four-dimensional spacetime rather than on a two-dimensional sheet[^1], but the potential energy landscape behaves in the same mathematical way: every mass carves a valley, and leaving it means climbing the slope and paying in kinetic energy.

## What a gravitational well is

In physics, the gravitational potential $\Phi(r)$ around a spherically symmetric mass $M$ at distance $r$ is defined as the work required per unit mass to bring an object from infinity (where potential is zero) to $r$[^2]:

$$\Phi(r) = - \frac{G M}{r}$$

where:

- $G \approx 6.6743 \times 10^{-11} \text{ m}^3\text{kg}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$ is Newton's gravitational constant.
- $M$ is the mass of the celestial body.
- $r$ is the radial distance from the center of mass.

The negative sign is paramount: it signifies a **bound state**. At infinitely far distances ($r \to \infty$), the potential approaches $0$. As you approach the mass ($r \to 0$), the potential plunges towards $-\infty$.

```{=html}
<script>
function updatePotentialWell() {
  const E = parseFloat(document.getElementById('well-slider-e').value);
  const L = parseFloat(document.getElementById('well-slider-l').value);

  document.getElementById('well-e-val').innerText = (E >= 0 ? '+' : '') + E.toFixed(2);
  document.getElementById('well-l-val').innerText = L.toFixed(2);

  // Exact physics calculations (normalized units GMm = 1, m = 1)
  const GMm = 1.0;
  const m = 1.0;
  
  // Potential minimum: r_min_well = L^2 / GMm
  const r_well_min = L > 0 ? (L * L) / GMm : 0;
  const U_well_min = L > 0 ? - (GMm * GMm) / (2 * L * L) : -Infinity;

  const uminEl = document.getElementById('readout-umin');
  uminEl.innerText = L > 0 ? U_well_min.toFixed(2) : '-∞ (Plunge)';

  // Calculate classical turning points: E = -GMm/r + L^2/(2m r^2)
  // 2E r^2 + 2GMm r - L^2 = 0
  const stateEl = document.getElementById('readout-state');
  const rminEl = document.getElementById('readout-rmin');
  const rmaxEl = document.getElementById('readout-rmax');

  let r1 = null;
  let r2 = null;

  if (L === 0) {
    stateEl.innerText = "Radial Plunge";
    stateEl.style.color = "#ef4444";
    rminEl.innerText = "0.00 (Crash)";
    rmaxEl.innerText = E < 0 ? (-GMm / E).toFixed(2) + " AU" : "∞ (Escape)";
  } else if (E < U_well_min) {
    stateEl.innerText = "Forbidden Energy";
    stateEl.style.color = "#94a3b8";
    rminEl.innerText = "N/A";
    rmaxEl.innerText = "N/A";
  } else if (Math.abs(E - U_well_min) < 0.01) {
    stateEl.innerText = "Circular Orbit";
    stateEl.style.color = "#38bdf8";
    rminEl.innerText = r_well_min.toFixed(2) + " AU";
    rmaxEl.innerText = r_well_min.toFixed(2) + " AU";
    r1 = r_well_min;
    r2 = r_well_min;
  } else if (E < 0) {
    // Bound elliptical orbit
    const disc = 4 * GMm * GMm + 8 * E * (L * L);
    if (disc >= 0) {
      const sqrtD = Math.sqrt(disc);
      r1 = (-2 * GMm + sqrtD) / (4 * E);
      r2 = (-2 * GMm - sqrtD) / (4 * E);
      if (r1 > r2) { const tmp = r1; r1 = r2; r2 = tmp; }
      stateEl.innerText = "Bound Ellipse";
      stateEl.style.color = "#10b981";
      rminEl.innerText = r1.toFixed(2) + " AU";
      rmaxEl.innerText = r2.toFixed(2) + " AU";
    }
  } else if (E === 0) {
    // Parabolic escape
    r1 = (L * L) / (2 * GMm);
    stateEl.innerText = "Parabolic Escape";
    stateEl.style.color = "#f59e0b";
    rminEl.innerText = r1.toFixed(2) + " AU";
    rmaxEl.innerText = "∞ (Zero v_inf)";
  } else {
    // Hyperbolic flyby
    const disc = 4 * GMm * GMm + 8 * E * (L * L);
    const sqrtD = Math.sqrt(disc);
    r1 = (-2 * GMm + sqrtD) / (4 * E);
    stateEl.innerText = "Hyperbolic Flyby";
    stateEl.style.color = "#8b5cf6";
    rminEl.innerText = r1.toFixed(2) + " AU";
    rmaxEl.innerText = "∞ (Unbound)";
  }

  drawPotentialWellCanvas(E, L, U_well_min, r1, r2);
}

function drawPotentialWellCanvas(E, L, U_min, r1, r2) {
  const canvas = document.getElementById('potential-well-canvas');
  if (!canvas) return;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

  const padLeft = 60, padRight = 30, padTop = 30, padBottom = 40;
  const w = canvas.width - padLeft - padRight;
  const h = canvas.height - padTop - padBottom;

  const rMinPlot = 0.35, rMaxPlot = 5.5;
  const uMinPlot = -1.2, uMaxPlot = 0.6;

  function toX(r) {
    return padLeft + ((r - rMinPlot) / (rMaxPlot - rMinPlot)) * w;
  }
  function toY(u) {
    return padTop + ((uMaxPlot - u) / (uMaxPlot - uMinPlot)) * h;
  }

  // Draw Grid Lines
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#1e293b';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  for (let r = 1; r <= 5; r++) {
    const gx = toX(r);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(gx, padTop); ctx.lineTo(gx, padTop + h); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#64748b';
    ctx.font = '11px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText(r + ' AU', gx - 12, padTop + h + 18);
  }
  for (let u = -1.0; u <= 0.5; u += 0.5) {
    const gy = toY(u);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(padLeft, gy); ctx.lineTo(padLeft + w, gy); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#64748b';
    ctx.font = '11px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText(u.toFixed(1), 16, gy + 4);
  }

  // Zero Energy Reference Line (E = 0)
  const yZero = toY(0);
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#475569';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
  ctx.setLineDash([6, 4]);
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(padLeft, yZero); ctx.lineTo(padLeft + w, yZero); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  ctx.fillStyle = '#94a3b8';
  ctx.font = '11px system-ui';
  ctx.fillText('Zero Energy (E = 0: Escape Threshold)', padLeft + w - 210, yZero - 6);

  // 1. Plot Pure Gravitational Potential (-1/r)
  ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(167, 139, 250, 0.4)';
  ctx.lineWidth = 2;
  ctx.beginPath();
  for (let r = rMinPlot; r <= rMaxPlot; r += 0.05) {
    const u_g = - 1.0 / r;
    const px = toX(r), py = toY(Math.max(uMinPlot - 0.2, u_g));
    if (r === rMinPlot) ctx.moveTo(px, py); else ctx.lineTo(px, py);
  }
  ctx.stroke();

  // 2. Plot Centrifugal Potential (L^2 / 2r^2)
  if (L > 0) {
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(52, 211, 153, 0.35)';
    ctx.lineWidth = 1.5;
    ctx.beginPath();
    for (let r = rMinPlot; r <= rMaxPlot; r += 0.05) {
      const u_c = (L * L) / (2 * r * r);
      if (u_c <= uMaxPlot + 0.2) {
        const px = toX(r), py = toY(u_c);
        if (r === rMinPlot) ctx.moveTo(px, py); else ctx.lineTo(px, py);
      }
    }
    ctx.stroke();
  }

  // 3. Shaded Bound Trapping Zone
  if (r1 !== null && r2 !== null && E < 0) {
    const x1 = Math.max(padLeft, toX(r1));
    const x2 = Math.min(padLeft + w, toX(r2));
    const yE = toY(E);

    ctx.fillStyle = 'rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.12)';
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(x1, yE);
    for (let r = r1; r <= r2; r += 0.02) {
      const u_eff = - 1.0 / r + (L * L) / (2 * r * r);
      ctx.lineTo(toX(r), toY(u_eff));
    }
    ctx.lineTo(x2, yE);
    ctx.closePath();
    ctx.fill();

    // Turning point markers
    ctx.fillStyle = '#38bdf8';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x1, yE, 5, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x2, yE, 5, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.font = '10px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('r_peri', x1 - 12, yE - 8);
    ctx.fillText('r_apo', x2 - 8, yE - 8);
  }

  // 4. Plot Effective Potential Curve U_eff(r)
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#38bdf8';
  ctx.lineWidth = 3.5;
  ctx.beginPath();
  let firstPoint = true;
  for (let r = rMinPlot; r <= rMaxPlot; r += 0.02) {
    const u_eff = - 1.0 / r + (L * L) / (2 * r * r);
    if (u_eff <= uMaxPlot + 0.5 && u_eff >= uMinPlot - 0.5) {
      const px = toX(r), py = toY(u_eff);
      if (firstPoint) { ctx.moveTo(px, py); firstPoint = false; } else ctx.lineTo(px, py);
    }
  }
  ctx.stroke();

  // 5. Total Energy Level E Horizontal Bar
  const yE = toY(E);
  if (yE >= padTop && yE <= padTop + h) {
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#f59e0b';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2.5;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(padLeft, yE);
    ctx.lineTo(padLeft + w, yE);
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#f59e0b';
    ctx.font = 'bold 11px system-ui';
    ctx.fillText('E = ' + (E >= 0 ? '+' : '') + E.toFixed(2), padLeft + 10, yE - 6);
  }
}

// Lifecycle registration
if (typeof document$ !== 'undefined') {
  document$.subscribe(() => {
    updatePotentialWell();
  });
}
window.addEventListener('load', updatePotentialWell);
setTimeout(updatePotentialWell, 200);
</script>
```


### Orbiting versus escaping

A spacecraft or particle of mass $m$ in this field has total mechanical energy:

$$E = K + U = \frac{1}{2} m v^2 - \frac{G M m}{r}$$

The sign of $E$ dictates its cosmic destiny:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Start["Particle with Total Energy E = K + U"] --> CheckE{"Total Energy E vs 0"}
    
    CheckE -- "E < 0 (Bound State)" --> SubBound{"Angular Momentum L"}
    SubBound -- "L > 0" --> Orbit["Elliptical / Circular Orbit (Trapped in Well)"]
    SubBound -- "L = 0" --> Plunge["Direct Radial Collision / Plunge"]
    
    CheckE -- "E = 0 (Parabolic)" --> EscapeZero["Parabolic Trajectory (Escapes to ∞ with v = 0)"]
    
    CheckE -- "E > 0 (Hyperbolic)" --> EscapePos["Hyperbolic Trajectory (Escapes with Residual Excess Velocity v_inf)"]

    class CheckE indigo
    class Orbit olive
    class Plunge rust
    class EscapeZero ochre
    class EscapePos plum
    classDef indigo fill:#1d4a62,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef plum fill:#48304a,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef rust fill:#a04b2d,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef olive fill:#5b6e34,stroke:#c97d62,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#ffffff
    classDef ochre fill:#d69a2e,stroke:#3b1a18,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#3b1a18
```

The minimum velocity needed at radius $r$ to reach $E = 0$ (climbing entirely out of the well to infinity) is the **escape velocity** $v_{\text{esc}}$:

$$\frac{1}{2} m v_{\text{esc}}^2 - \frac{G M m}{r} = 0 \implies v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 G M}{r}}$$


### The three archetypes side by side

| Feature | Earth (Rocky Planet) | Black Hole (Stellar Mass) | Binary Massive Planets |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mass Structure** | Single distributed sphere ($M_\oplus \approx 5.97 \times 10^{24}\text{ kg}$) | Point singularity / compressed horizon ($M \ge 3 M_\odot$) | Two interacting masses ($M_1, M_2$) orbiting a barycentre |
| **Well Bottom** | Truncated at physical surface ($r = R_\oplus \approx 6,371\text{ km}$) | Singular abyss ($r = 0$), shielded by event horizon $r_s$ | Two distinct funnels joined by an $L_1$ saddle bridge |
| **Surface Potential** | $\Phi_{\text{surf}} \approx -62.5\text{ MJ/kg}$ | $\Phi(r_s) \to -c^2 / 2$ (relativistic limit) | Variable $\Phi(x, y)$ with saddle barriers |
| **Escape Velocity** | $11.19\text{ km/s}$ at sea level | $c \approx 299,792\text{ km/s}$ at $r = r_s$ | Dependent on location and launch vector |
| **Equilibrium Points** | Center of mass only ($r = 0$) | Singular center ($r = 0$) | 5 Lagrange equilibrium points ($L_1 \dots L_5$) |
| **Relativistic Warping** | Negligible ($\approx 1.4 \times 10^{-9}$ fractional redshift) | Extreme (infinite time dilation, photon sphere at $1.5 r_s$) | Moderate to high depending on stellar/planetary masses |

## Three wells compared

### Earth, a well with a floor

For Earth, the potential does not plunge to $-\infty$. Because Earth is a solid sphere of radius $R_\oplus$, the $1/r$ potential stops decreasing at the surface. Inside the Earth (assuming uniform density $\rho$), Gauss's Law dictates that gravity decreases linearly to zero at the center:

$$\Phi(r) = \begin{cases} -\frac{G M}{R_\oplus} \left( \frac{3}{2} - \frac{r^2}{2 R_\oplus^2} \right) & \text{for } r < R_\oplus \\ -\frac{G M}{r} & \text{for } r \ge R_\oplus \end{cases}$$

```
Earth's Gravitational Potential Cross-Section:
        r = -R⊕           r = 0           r = +R⊕
═══════════╤════════════════╤════════════════╤═══════════ Φ = 0 (Deep Space)
            \              / \              /
             \            /   \            /
              \          /     \          /
  1/r curve    \        /       \        /   1/r curve
                \      /         \      /
                 \____/           \____/
                 Solid Surface (r = R⊕)
                 Depth = -62.5 MJ/kg
                 v_esc = 11.2 km/s
```

#### The rocket equation

To climb out of Earth's $62.5\text{ MJ/kg}$ energy ditch, a rocket must burn propellant according to Tsiolkovsky's rocket equation[^3]:

$$\Delta v = v_e \ln \left( \frac{m_0}{m_f} \right)$$

Because propellant itself has mass, the fuel fraction grows exponentially with the depth of the well:

```
Mass Breakdown of a Moon/Mars-Bound Rocket Launching from Earth:
[█████████████████████████████████████████████████░░] 94% Propellant (Fuel & Oxidizer)
[██                                                 ]  4% Rocket Dry Structure & Engines
[█                                                  ]  2% Actual Scientific Payload
```

### A black hole, a well with no floor

A black hole represents a gravity well with no solid surface to stop the plunge. According to Einstein's General Relativity, spacetime curvature near a Schwarzschild black hole[^4] creates key relativistic boundaries that do not exist in Newtonian gravity:

```{=html}
</svg>
<figcaption><strong>Figure 1 | A black hole's well has no floor, and the landmark radii sit at fixed fractions of its depth.</strong> Matching the Schwarzschild metric term $g_{tt} = -(1 - r_s/r)$ to $-(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)$ gives $\Phi/c^2 = -r_s/2r$ exactly, so the profile above is the real curve rather than a sketch. Because that depth is set purely by $r/r_s$, the innermost stable circular orbit always sits at $-1/6$, the photon sphere at $-1/3$, and the horizon at $-1/2$ — for a stellar-mass hole and a supermassive one alike. Unlike Earth, whose $1/r$ curve is truncated by a solid surface at $-62.5\text{ MJ kg}^{-1}$, nothing here stops the descent: inside $r_s$ (magenta) no static observer can exist, so no potential can be defined and every worldline runs to $r = 0$.</figcaption>
</figure>
```


1. **Innermost Stable Circular Orbit (ISCO, $r = 3 r_s = \frac{6GM}{c^2}$)**: Inside this radius, no stable circular orbits exist. Any perturbation causes matter to spiral precipitously inward.
2. **Photon Sphere ($r = 1.5 r_s = \frac{3GM}{c^2}$)**: Photons (light) can orbit the black hole in unstable circular orbits. A camera placed here would look forward and see the back of its own housing.
3. **Event Horizon ($r = r_s = \frac{2GM}{c^2}$)**: The boundary of no return. Space itself flows inward faster than light; all null geodesics point inward toward $r=0$. Rotating Kerr black holes introduce an additional ergosphere boundary outside the horizon[^5].

### A binary system, two wells and a saddle

When two massive bodies orbit a common center of mass, their gravitational potential wells overlap in the co-rotating frame. The **effective potential** (accounting for both gravitational attraction and centrifugal acceleration) creates an intricate landscape with two deep funnels connected by a saddle pass, originally solved in the restricted three-body problem by Joseph-Louis Lagrange[^6]:

$$\Phi_{\text{eff}}(\mathbf{r}) = -\frac{G M_1}{|\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_1|} - \frac{G M_2}{|\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_2|} - \frac{1}{2} (\boldsymbol{\omega} \times \mathbf{r})^2$$

```
Two Massive Planets Potential Profile (Cross-Section through Centers):

        L3               Planet 1             L1            Planet 2            L2
   ═══/\════════════════════╤═════════════════/\═══════════════╤════════════════/\═══
     /  \                  / \               /  \             / \              /  \
    /    \                /   \             /    \           /   \            /    \
   /      \              /     \           /      \         /     \          /      \
           \            /       \         /        \       /       \        /
            \          /         \       /          \     /         \      /
             \        /           \     /            \   /           \    /
              \______/             \___/              \_/             \__/
               Well 1                                  Well 2
              (Mass M1)             L1 Saddle        (Mass M2)
                                 (Gravitational Pass)
```

| Lagrange Point | Geometric Position | Potential Topography | Dynamic Stability | Real-World Astro & Space Missions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$L_1$** | Between $M_1$ and $M_2$ | **Saddle point** (dip along perpendicular axis, peak along line of centers) | Unstable (requires station-keeping) | SOHO solar observatory (Sun-Earth), Inter-planetary transfer corridor |
| **$L_2$** | Beyond $M_2$ along the line of centers | **Saddle point** | Unstable | James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Gaia, WMAP |
| **$L_3$** | Beyond $M_1$ opposite to $M_2$ | **Saddle point** | Unstable | Sci-Fi "Counter-Earth", theoretical resonance studies |
| **$L_4$** | Vertex of equilateral triangle ($+60^\circ$ ahead) | **Effective potential hill** | Stable (Coriolis force circles particles around peak) | Jupiter Trojans (Greeks), Earth Trojan 2020 XL5, Lucy mission |
| **$L_5$** | Vertex of equilateral triangle ($-60^\circ$ behind) | **Effective potential hill** | Stable (Coriolis stabilized) | Jupiter Trojans, proposed space habitats |

### Escape conditions across the three regimes

The escape condition takes a different form in each regime:

$$v_{\text{esc}}(r) = \begin{cases} \sqrt{\frac{2 G M_\oplus}{R_\oplus}} \approx 11.2\text{ km/s} & \text{(Earth Surface)} \\ c \sqrt{\frac{r_s}{r}} \implies c \text{ at } r = r_s & \text{(Schwarzschild Black Hole)} \\ \sqrt{2 \left(\Phi_{\text{eff}}(L_1) - \Phi_{\text{eff}}(\mathbf{r}_0)\right)} & \text{(Inter-well Transit between Binary Planets)} \end{cases}$$

#### The payload dilemma for any well

To leave any gravitational well of depth $\Delta \Phi = \frac{1}{2} v_{\text{esc}}^2$, the required propellant-to-payload ratio $\frac{m_{\text{fuel}}}{m_{\text{payload}}}$ for an exhaust velocity $c_e$ is:

$$\frac{m_{\text{fuel}}}{m_{\text{payload}}} = \exp\left( \frac{\sqrt{2 \Delta \Phi}}{c_e} \right) - 1$$

As the potential well deepens linearly, the fuel required grows **exponentially**. On a super-Earth with just $2\times$ Earth's radius and mass, the rocket equation makes chemical spaceflight virtually impossible — underscoring how delicate Earth's gravitational cradle truly is.

```{=html}
<script>
// --- PLOTLY 3D GRAVITY WELL VISUALIZER ---
let currentSystem = 'earth';
let binaryRatio = 0.35;

function generatePotentialGrid(type, ratio) {
  const N = 50;
  const x = [];
  const y = [];
  const z = [];
  const range = 6.0;
  
  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    x.push(-range + (2 * range * i) / (N - 1));
    y.push(-range + (2 * range * i) / (N - 1));
  }

  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    const row = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < N; j++) {
      const px = x[j];
      const py = y[i];
      let val = 0;

      if (type === 'earth') {
        const r = Math.sqrt(px * px + py * py);
        const R_earth = 1.2;
        if (r < R_earth) {
          val = - (1.0 / R_earth) * (1.5 - 0.5 * (r * r) / (R_earth * R_earth));
        } else {
          val = - 1.0 / r;
        }
        val = Math.max(val, -1.8);
      } else if (type === 'bh') {
        const r = Math.sqrt(px * px + py * py);
        const r_s = 0.6;
        if (r <= r_s * 0.5) {
          val = -5.0;
        } else {
          // Relativistic effective potential approximation
          val = - 1.5 / Math.pow(r, 1.15) - 0.5 * (r_s * r_s) / Math.pow(r, 3);
          val = Math.max(val, -5.0);
        }
      } else if (type === 'binary') {
        const d = 2.4;
        const x1 = -d * ratio / (1.0 + ratio);
        const x2 = d / (1.0 + ratio);
        const r1 = Math.sqrt((px - x1) * (px - x1) + py * py);
        const r2 = Math.sqrt((px - x2) * (px - x2) + py * py);
        
        const pot1 = - 1.8 / Math.max(r1, 0.45);
        const pot2 = - (1.8 * ratio) / Math.max(r2, 0.35);
        
        // Co-rotating centrifugal potential: -0.5 * omega^2 * (px^2 + py^2)
        const omegaSq = 0.08;
        const rot = - 0.5 * omegaSq * (px * px + py * py);
        
        val = pot1 + pot2 + rot;
        val = Math.max(val, -4.5);
      }
      row.push(val);
    }
    z.push(row);
  }
  return { x, y, z };
}

function plotGravityWell() {
  const dataGrid = generatePotentialGrid(currentSystem, binaryRatio);
  
  let titleText = "Gravitational Potential Well: Earth (Truncated Core)";
  let colorscale = 'Viridis';
  
  if (currentSystem === 'bh') {
    titleText = "Relativistic Potential Funnel: Black Hole (r_s Horizon & Singular Abyss)";
    colorscale = 'Electric';
  } else if (currentSystem === 'binary') {
    titleText = "Binary System Potential: Roche Lobes & Lagrange Saddles (L1 - L5)";
    colorscale = 'Plasma';
  }

  const surfaceTrace = {
    z: dataGrid.z,
    x: dataGrid.x,
    y: dataGrid.y,
    type: 'surface',
    colorscale: colorscale,
    showscale: true,
    colorbar: {
      title: 'Potential Φ',
      titleside: 'top',
      thickness: 14,
      len: 0.7,
      tickfont: { color: '#94a3b8' },
      titlefont: { color: '#f8fafc' }
    },
    contours: {
      z: {
        show: true,
        usecolormap: true,
        highlightcolor: "#00f0ff",
        project: { z: true }
      }
    },
    lighting: {
      ambient: 0.65,
      diffuse: 0.8,
      specular: 0.3
    }
  };

  const layout = {
    title: {
      text: titleText,
      font: { color: '#f1f5f9', size: 15 }
    },
    paper_bgcolor: '#0f172a',
    plot_bgcolor: '#0f172a',
    margin: { l: 20, r: 20, b: 20, t: 40 },
    scene: {
      xaxis: { title: 'X Distance', color: '#94a3b8', gridcolor: '#334155', zerolinecolor: '#475569' },
      yaxis: { title: 'Y Distance', color: '#94a3b8', gridcolor: '#334155', zerolinecolor: '#475569' },
      zaxis: { title: 'Potential Energy Φ', color: '#94a3b8', gridcolor: '#334155', zerolinecolor: '#475569' },
      camera: {
        eye: { x: 1.4, y: -1.5, z: 1.2 }
      }
    }
  };

  const config = { responsive: true, displayModeBar: true, displaylogo: false };
  Plotly.react('plotly-gravity-well', [surfaceTrace], layout, config);
}

function selectSystem(sys) {
  currentSystem = sys;
  const btnEarth = document.getElementById('btn-earth');
  const btnBh = document.getElementById('btn-bh');
  const btnBinary = document.getElementById('btn-binary');
  const caption = document.getElementById('system-caption');
  const massCtrl = document.getElementById('mass-ratio-control');

  btnEarth.style.background = '#334155';
  btnBh.style.background = '#334155';
  btnBinary.style.background = '#334155';

  if (sys === 'earth') {
    btnEarth.style.background = '#2563eb';
    caption.innerText = 'Single planet: Truncated potential with solid surface cutoff.';
    massCtrl.style.display = 'none';
  } else if (sys === 'bh') {
    btnBh.style.background = '#8b5cf6';
    caption.innerText = 'Black hole: Deep relativistic funnel with event horizon plunge.';
    massCtrl.style.display = 'none';
  } else if (sys === 'binary') {
    btnBinary.style.background = '#f59e0b';
    caption.innerText = 'Binary system: Double funnel with L1 saddle bridge and Lagrange points.';
    massCtrl.style.display = 'flex';
  }
  plotGravityWell();
}

function updateBinaryMass(val) {
  binaryRatio = parseFloat(val);
  document.getElementById('massRatioVal').innerText = binaryRatio.toFixed(2);
  plotGravityWell();
}

// --- 2D CANVAS ORBITAL SIMULATOR ---
let simScene = 'earth';
let probe = null;
let trail = [];
let animId = null;
let simTime = 0;
let probeOrigin = { x: 380, y: 110 };

// Auto-running ambient satellites so the sandbox is lively by default
let ambientSatellites = [];

function initAmbientSatellites() {
  ambientSatellites = [];
  if (simScene === 'earth') {
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 0, radius: 70, speed: 0.022, color: '#38bdf8', size: 3.5, label: 'LEO Satellite' });
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 2.1, radius: 125, speed: 0.009, color: '#a78bfa', size: 3.5, label: 'GEO Satellite' });
  } else if (simScene === 'bh') {
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 0.5, radius: 45, speed: 0.045, color: '#f59e0b', size: 3, label: 'Accretion Disk' });
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 3.2, radius: 90, speed: 0.016, color: '#ec4899', size: 3.5, label: 'Stable Relativistic Orbit' });
  } else if (simScene === 'binary') {
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 0, radius: 55, speed: 0.025, center: { x: 260, y: 210 }, color: '#38bdf8', size: 3, label: 'Moon 1' });
    ambientSatellites.push({ angle: 1.5, radius: 42, speed: 0.03, center: { x: 500, y: 210 }, color: '#fbbf24', size: 3, label: 'Moon 2' });
  }
}

function getCanvasAndContext() {
  const canvas = document.getElementById('gravity-sandbox');
  if (!canvas) return null;
  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
  return { canvas, ctx };
}

function setSimScene(scene) {
  simScene = scene;
  initAmbientSatellites();
  resetSim();

  const v0Input = document.getElementById('sim-v0');
  const angleInput = document.getElementById('sim-angle');

  if (scene === 'earth') {
    if (v0Input) v0Input.value = 5.8;
    if (angleInput) angleInput.value = 90;
    probeOrigin = { x: 380, y: 110 };
  } else if (scene === 'bh') {
    if (v0Input) v0Input.value = 6.5;
    if (angleInput) angleInput.value = 100;
    probeOrigin = { x: 380, y: 90 };
  } else if (scene === 'binary') {
    if (v0Input) v0Input.value = 4.2;
    if (angleInput) angleInput.value = 85;
    probeOrigin = { x: 230, y: 120 };
  }
  updateSimControls();
}

function updateSimControls() {
  const v0Input = document.getElementById('sim-v0');
  const angleInput = document.getElementById('sim-angle');
  const v0Display = document.getElementById('v0-display');
  const angleDisplay = document.getElementById('angle-display');

  if (v0Input && v0Display) {
    v0Display.innerText = parseFloat(v0Input.value).toFixed(1);
  }
  if (angleInput && angleDisplay) {
    angleDisplay.innerText = angleInput.value;
  }
}

function setupCanvasEvents() {
  const canvas = document.getElementById('gravity-sandbox');
  if (!canvas || canvas.dataset.hasEvents) return;
  canvas.dataset.hasEvents = "true";

  canvas.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    const rect = canvas.getBoundingClientRect();
    const scaleX = canvas.width / rect.width;
    const scaleY = canvas.height / rect.height;
    probeOrigin.x = (e.clientX - rect.left) * scaleX;
    probeOrigin.y = (e.clientY - rect.top) * scaleY;
    resetSim();
  });
}

function resetSim() {
  probe = null;
  trail = [];
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
  const energyEl = document.getElementById('energy-display');
  if (statusEl) {
    statusEl.innerText = 'Ready to Launch';
    statusEl.style.color = '#38bdf8';
  }
  if (energyEl) {
    energyEl.innerText = '--';
  }
}

function clearTrails() {
  trail = [];
}

function launchProbe() {
  const v0Input = document.getElementById('sim-v0');
  const angleInput = document.getElementById('sim-angle');
  const v0 = v0Input ? parseFloat(v0Input.value) : 5.8;
  const angleDeg = angleInput ? parseFloat(angleInput.value) : 90;
  const angleRad = (angleDeg * Math.PI) / 180;

  const speedScale = 0.55;
  const vx = v0 * Math.cos(angleRad) * speedScale;
  const vy = - v0 * Math.sin(angleRad) * speedScale;

  probe = {
    x: probeOrigin.x,
    y: probeOrigin.y,
    vx: vx,
    vy: vy,
    active: true,
    state: 'flying'
  };

  trail = [{ x: probe.x, y: probe.y, state: 'flying' }];
  const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
  if (statusEl) {
    statusEl.innerText = 'In Orbit / Active Flight';
    statusEl.style.color = '#10b981';
  }
}

function animStep() {
  simTime += 0.016;

  // 1. Update ambient satellites continuously
  ambientSatellites.forEach(sat => {
    sat.angle += sat.speed;
  });

  // 2. Physics integration for user-launched probe
  if (probe && probe.active) {
    const dt = 0.25;
    const subSteps = 4;
    let currentPotential = -100;
    
    for (let step = 0; step < subSteps; step++) {
      let ax = 0;
      let ay = 0;

      if (simScene === 'earth') {
        const cx = 380, cy = 210, GMe = 1800;
        const dx = cx - probe.x;
        const dy = cy - probe.y;
        const r = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);
        
        if (r < 32) {
          probe.active = false;
          probe.state = 'crashed';
          const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
          if (statusEl) {
            statusEl.innerText = 'Surface Impact / Plunge';
            statusEl.style.color = '#ef4444';
          }
          break;
        }
        
        const force = GMe / (r * r);
        ax += force * (dx / r);
        ay += force * (dy / r);
        currentPotential = - GMe / r;

      } else if (simScene === 'bh') {
        const cx = 380, cy = 210, GMbh = 3200, rs = 22;
        const dx = cx - probe.x;
        const dy = cy - probe.y;
        const r = Math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy);

        if (r <= rs) {
          probe.active = false;
          probe.state = 'swallowed';
          const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
          if (statusEl) {
            statusEl.innerText = 'Crossed Event Horizon (Trapped Forever)';
            statusEl.style.color = '#ef4444';
          }
          break;
        }

        const effectiveDist = Math.max(r - rs, 2.0);
        const force = GMbh / (effectiveDist * effectiveDist);
        ax += force * (dx / r);
        ay += force * (dy / r);
        currentPotential = - GMbh / effectiveDist;

      } else if (simScene === 'binary') {
        const c1x = 260, c1y = 210, GM1 = 1500, R1 = 28;
        const c2x = 500, c2y = 210, GM2 = 900, R2 = 20;

        const dx1 = c1x - probe.x, dy1 = c1y - probe.y, r1 = Math.sqrt(dx1*dx1 + dy1*dy1);
        const dx2 = c2x - probe.x, dy2 = c2y - probe.y, r2 = Math.sqrt(dx2*dx2 + dy2*dy2);

        if (r1 < R1 || r2 < R2) {
          probe.active = false;
          probe.state = 'crashed';
          const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
          if (statusEl) {
            statusEl.innerText = 'Planet Surface Collision';
            statusEl.style.color = '#ef4444';
          }
          break;
        }

        ax += (GM1 / (r1 * r1)) * (dx1 / r1) + (GM2 / (r2 * r2)) * (dx2 / r2);
        ay += (GM1 / (r1 * r1)) * (dy1 / r1) + (GM2 / (r2 * r2)) * (dy2 / r2);
        currentPotential = - GM1/r1 - GM2/r2;
      }

      probe.vx += ax * (dt / subSteps);
      probe.vy += ay * (dt / subSteps);
      probe.x += probe.vx * (dt / subSteps);
      probe.y += probe.vy * (dt / subSteps);

      if (probe.x < -100 || probe.x > 860 || probe.y < -100 || probe.y > 520) {
        probe.active = false;
        probe.state = 'escaped';
        const statusEl = document.getElementById('sim-status');
        if (statusEl) {
          statusEl.innerText = 'Escaped to Deep Space (E > 0)';
          statusEl.style.color = '#f59e0b';
        }
        break;
      }
    }

    if (probe) {
      trail.push({ x: probe.x, y: probe.y, state: probe.state });
      if (trail.length > 800) trail.shift();

      const speedSq = probe.vx * probe.vx + probe.vy * probe.vy;
      const kinetic = 0.5 * speedSq * 10;
      const totalEnergy = kinetic + currentPotential;
      const energyEl = document.getElementById('energy-display');
      if (energyEl) {
        energyEl.innerText = `${totalEnergy > 0 ? '+' : ''}${totalEnergy.toFixed(1)} J/kg`;
      }
    }
  }

  drawScene();
  animId = requestAnimationFrame(animStep);
}

function drawScene() {
  const handles = getCanvasAndContext();
  if (!handles) return;
  const { canvas, ctx } = handles;

  ctx.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);

  // 1. Spacetime metric background grid
  ctx.strokeStyle = '#0f172a';
  ctx.lineWidth = 1;
  for (let gx = 0; gx < canvas.width; gx += 40) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(gx, 0); ctx.lineTo(gx, canvas.height); ctx.stroke();
  }
  for (let gy = 0; gy < canvas.height; gy += 40) {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, gy); ctx.lineTo(canvas.width, gy); ctx.stroke();
  }

  // 2. Draw celestial bodies
  if (simScene === 'earth') {
    const cx = 380, cy = 210, r = 32;
    const grad = ctx.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, r*0.8, cx, cy, r*2.2);
    grad.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.4)');
    grad.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(59, 130, 246, 0)');
    ctx.fillStyle = grad;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, r*2.2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#1e40af';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, r, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#60a5fa';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.stroke();
    
    ctx.fillStyle = '#93c5fd';
    ctx.font = '12px system-ui, sans-serif';
    ctx.fillText('🌍 Earth (R = 6,371 km)', cx - 60, cy + r + 18);

  } else if (simScene === 'bh') {
    const cx = 380, cy = 210, rs = 22;
    
    const grad = ctx.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, rs, cx, cy, rs*3.5);
    grad.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.5)');
    grad.addColorStop(0.5, 'rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.2)');
    grad.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)');
    ctx.fillStyle = grad;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, rs*3.5, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#f59e0b';
    ctx.setLineDash([4, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, rs*1.5, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);

    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.4)';
    ctx.setLineDash([2, 4]);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, rs*3.0, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#000000';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(cx, cy, rs, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#ef4444';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#fca5a5';
    ctx.font = '12px system-ui, sans-serif';
    ctx.fillText('🕳️ Event Horizon (r_s)', cx - 55, cy + rs + 18);
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fde68a';
    ctx.fillText('Photon Sphere (1.5 r_s)', cx + rs*1.5 + 8, cy - 6);

  } else if (simScene === 'binary') {
    const c1x = 260, c1y = 210, r1 = 28;
    const c2x = 500, c2y = 210, r2 = 20;

    const l1x = 380, l1y = 210;
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ef4444';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(l1x, l1y, 4, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fca5a5';
    ctx.font = '11px system-ui, sans-serif';
    ctx.fillText('L1 (Saddle)', l1x - 24, l1y - 8);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#0284c7';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c1x, c1y, r1, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#38bdf8'; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#bae6fd';
    ctx.fillText('Planet 1 (M1)', c1x - 30, c1y + r1 + 16);

    ctx.fillStyle = '#d97706';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(c2x, c2y, r2, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#fbbf24'; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = '#fde68a';
    ctx.fillText('Planet 2 (M2)', c2x - 30, c2y + r2 + 16);
  }

  // 3. Draw auto-running ambient satellites and their orbital tracks
  ambientSatellites.forEach(sat => {
    const center = sat.center || { x: 380, y: 210 };
    const sx = center.x + sat.radius * Math.cos(sat.angle);
    const sy = center.y + sat.radius * Math.sin(sat.angle);

    // Orbit path ring
    ctx.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)';
    ctx.setLineDash([3, 5]);
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(center.x, center.y, sat.radius, 0, Math.PI * 2);
    ctx.stroke();
    ctx.setLineDash([]);

    // Glowing satellite body
    ctx.fillStyle = sat.color;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(sx, sy, sat.size, 0, Math.PI * 2);
    ctx.fill();

    // Satellite label
    ctx.fillStyle = '#94a3b8';
    ctx.font = '10px system-ui, sans-serif';
    ctx.fillText(sat.label, sx + 6, sy - 4);
  });

  // 4. Draw user-launched probe trajectory
  if (trail.length > 1) {
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    for (let i = 1; i < trail.length; i++) {
      ctx.beginPath();
      ctx.moveTo(trail[i-1].x, trail[i-1].y);
      ctx.lineTo(trail[i].x, trail[i].y);
      
      const alpha = Math.min(1.0, i / trail.length);
      if (trail[i].state === 'crashed' || trail[i].state === 'swallowed') {
        ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(239, 68, 68, ${alpha})`;
      } else if (trail[i].state === 'escaped') {
        ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(245, 158, 11, ${alpha})`;
      } else {
        ctx.strokeStyle = `rgba(16, 185, 129, ${alpha})`;
      }
      ctx.stroke();
    }
  }

  // 5. Draw launch origin marker and aim preview arrow
  if (!probe || !probe.active) {
    ctx.fillStyle = '#38bdf8';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(probeOrigin.x, probeOrigin.y, 5, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();

    const v0Input = document.getElementById('sim-v0');
    const angleInput = document.getElementById('sim-angle');
    const v0 = v0Input ? parseFloat(v0Input.value) : 5.8;
    const angleDeg = angleInput ? parseFloat(angleInput.value) : 90;
    const angleRad = (angleDeg * Math.PI) / 180;
    const arrowLen = v0 * 6.5;
    const targetX = probeOrigin.x + arrowLen * Math.cos(angleRad);
    const targetY = probeOrigin.y - arrowLen * Math.sin(angleRad);

    ctx.strokeStyle = '#38bdf8';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2;
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(probeOrigin.x, probeOrigin.y);
    ctx.lineTo(targetX, targetY);
    ctx.stroke();

    ctx.fillStyle = '#38bdf8';
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.arc(targetX, targetY, 3, 0, Math.PI*2);
    ctx.fill();
  }

  // 6. Draw user-launched probe
  if (probe && probe.active) {
    ctx.fillStyle = '#ffffff';
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(probe.x, probe.y, 4.5, 0, Math.PI*2); ctx.fill();
    ctx.strokeStyle = '#10b981';
    ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.stroke();
  }
}

function startSimulationLoop() {
  if (animId) cancelAnimationFrame(animId);
  initAmbientSatellites();
  setupCanvasEvents();
  animId = requestAnimationFrame(animStep);
}

function initAllVisuals() {
  if (typeof Plotly !== 'undefined') {
    plotGravityWell();
  }
  startSimulationLoop();
}

// Attach to lifecycle
if (typeof document$ !== 'undefined') {
  document$.subscribe(() => {
    initAllVisuals();
  });
}

window.addEventListener('load', () => {
  initAllVisuals();
});

// Immediate execution fallback
setTimeout(() => {
  initAllVisuals();
}, 250);
</script>
```


### Data and code availability

- **Interactive Simulations**: All 3D potential visualizers and 2D orbital sandboxes are implemented in client-side HTML5 Canvas and Plotly.js, self-contained within this post.
- **Source Code**: Mathematical derivation notebooks and source files are hosted on GitHub: [`kamingfung/kamingfung.github.io`](https://github.com/kamingfung/kamingfung.github.io).
- **Physical Constants**: Planetary and astrophysical parameters follow the standard CODATA/IAU recommended constants[^7].

## Key takeaways

- A gravitational well is the potential $\Phi(r) = -GM/r$; the sign of the total energy $E = K + U$ decides whether a body is bound ($E < 0$), parabolic ($E = 0$) or escapes ($E > 0$), and $v_{\text{esc}} = \sqrt{2GM/r}$ is the speed that makes $E = 0$.
- Earth's well stops at its surface, $62.5\text{ MJ kg}^{-1}$ deep; the rocket equation $\Delta v = v_e \ln(m_0/m_f)$ turns that fixed depth into an exponential fuel fraction, which is why a launch vehicle is about 94% propellant.
- A Schwarzschild black hole's well has no floor, and because its depth depends only on $r/r_s$ the ISCO, photon sphere and horizon sit at $-1/6$, $-1/3$ and $-1/2$ of $c^2$ for any mass.
- Two orbiting masses produce a double well whose effective potential has five equilibria: three collinear saddle points ($L_1$ to $L_3$, unstable) and two triangular hills ($L_4$, $L_5$) stabilised by the Coriolis force when $M_1/M_2 > 24.96$.
- Deepening a well linearly raises the fuel needed to leave it exponentially; a super-Earth twice our radius and mass would make chemical spaceflight impractical.

[^1]: Misner, C. W., Thorne, K. S. & Wheeler, J. A. *Gravitation*. (W. H. Freeman, San Francisco, 1973). https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400889099
[^2]: Newton, I. *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica*. (J. Streater, London, 1687). https://doi.org/10.5479/sil.288219.39088015628391
[^3]: Tsiolkovsky, K. E. Exploration of outer space by means of rocket devices. *Nauchnoe Obozrenie* **5**, 45–75 (1903).
[^4]: Schwarzschild, K. Über das Gravitationsfeld eines Massenpunktes nach der Einsteinschen Theorie. *Sitzungsber. Preuss. Akad. Wiss.* **1916**, 189–196 (1916).
[^5]: Kerr, R. P. Gravitational field of a spinning mass as an example of algebraically special metrics. *Phys. Rev. Lett.* **11**, 237–238 (1963). https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237
[^6]: Lagrange, J. L. Essai sur le problème des trois corps. *Prix de l'Académie Royale des Sciences de Paris* **9**, 292 (1772).
[^7]: Tiesinga, E., Mohr, P. J., Newell, D. B. & Taylor, B. N. CODATA recommended values of the fundamental physical constants: 2018. *Rev. Mod. Phys.* **93**, 025010 (2021). https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.93.025010
